title: Novel creatine formulation exhibits similar serum creatine concentrations and pharmacokinetics to creatine monohydrate in healthy adults.
authors: DelBiondo GM, Gottlieb CW, Baker PA, Johnson WM, Kelly CG, Smith-Ryan AE
journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: BACKGROUND: Creatine monohydrate (CrM) is the most widely studied creatine form, demonstrating robust efficacy, bioavailability, and safety. With creatine growing in popularity, alternative formulations of creatine have been developed to target solubility and to optimize absorption pharmacokinetics (PK), as well as to reduce gastrointestinal (GI) intolerability. The purpose of the current study was to evaluate the acute effects of a novel creatine monohydrate (OptiCreatineTM; CrO) compared to CrM on serum creatine PK and GI tolerability in healthy adults. METHODS: Healthy, recreationally active adults (age: 22 ± 3 years; males n = 8, females n = 9) consumed a single 5-gram dose of CrM or CrO across two separate visits following an overnight fast, in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. Venous blood samples were collected at baseline and 30, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, and 300 mins post-ingestion of their assigned treatment to assess serum creatine concentrations. PK parameters including peak concentration (Cmax), time to peak (Tmax), absorption rate constant (ka), elimination rate constant (kel; h-1), and area under the curve (AUC₀-T) were derived using nonlinear regression modeling. GI symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires. RESULTS: There was no difference in serum creatine concentrations between CrM or CrO across all participants (p = 0.707), males (p = 0.318), or females (p = 0.996) at any time point. Serum creatine increased over time regardless of treatment (p < 0.0001). No differences were observed between CrM and CrO for Cmax (mean difference ± standard deviation (MD ± SD): 7.66 ± 50.37μM; p = 0.82), Tmax (MD ± SD: -0.04 ± 0.13 h; p = 0.54), ka (MD ± SD: -0.15 ± 0.45 h-1; p = 0.51), kel (MD ± SD: 0.01 ± 0.03 h-1; p = 0.61), or AUC₀-T (MD ± SD: 22.09 ± 160.57 μM·h; p = 0.74), with no sex × treatment interactions (p ≥ 0.05). Descriptive evaluation showed similar GI symptom profiles between conditions, with low frequency and minimal severity reported across both treatments. CONCLUSIONS: A single 5-gram dose of CrO produced similar serum creatine and PK characteristics to CrM in healthy adults. These findings support CrO as a viable delivery option, with no significant differences in acute pharmacokinetic profiles or GI tolerability compared to CrM.

title: From detection to prediction: AI-integrated molecular and biosensing approaches for psychrotrophic and thermophilic spoilage bacteria in dairy systems.
authors: Shamlan A, Khan MU, Farid A, Huo S, Liu H, Chen Z
abstract: Psychrotrophic Gram-negative bacteria and thermophilic or thermoduric spore-forming bacteria are major causes of quality deterioration and shelf-life loss in milk and dairy products. Their impact is mediated primarily by heat-stable peptidases and lipases, heat-resistant spores and biofilms that persist in processing environments; with the notable exception of toxigenic members of the Bacillus cereus group, most of these organisms are spoilage rather than safety hazards. Culture-based methods remain the reference standard but are slow and provide single time-point information. This review critically evaluates molecular and sensing methods, including quantitative and digital PCR, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-Cas assays, biosensors, viability assays, spectroscopy and (meta)omics, with explicit attention to whether performance has been demonstrated in naturally contaminated dairy matrices rather than in buffer or spiked samples, and examines how their outputs could inform predictive microbiology and machine learning. A classification framework based on growth-temperature range, heat resistance, sporulation and dairy relevance is provided, and each detection-to-prediction pathway is graded as demonstrated in dairy, partly demonstrated or proposed. Validated dairy applications currently exist mainly for individual detection assays and for mechanistic or stochastic shelf-life models driven by culture-derived data; prospective, validated workflows in which molecular or biosensor outputs are used as model inputs to forecast spoilage have not yet been reported. Because heat-stable enzymes can spoil ultra-high-temperature products after the producing cells have been inactivated, viable counts alone are insufficient predictors of such defects. Key barriers include matrix effects, small and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, limited external validation and poorly defined intended use. Detection-to-prediction integration should therefore be regarded as an emerging research direction rather than an established industrial capability.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
authors: Guo J, Peng Y, Xiao X, Li S, Zhu J, Lin J, Li J, Wu D
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Microenvironmental barriers to healing in osteoradionecrosis and opportunities for regenerative intervention.
authors: La Croix AE, Torres Gouveia ME, Bertone PM, Nemanic NM, Bahney CS, Hixon KR
abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

title: Role of protein lactylation in pulmonary and cardiovascular diseases: Current research and future perspectives (Review).
authors: Pan ZA, Tong LT, Wang ZM
abstract: The cardiopulmonary system is highly coupled in structure and function. Metabolic and epigenetic disturbances constitute the common pathological basis for the progression of cardiopulmonary diseases and their comorbidities. Aberrant metabolic reprogramming triggers lactate accumulation. As a novel post-translational modification, protein lactylation participates in the regulation of inflammatory responses, cell death and fibrotic remodeling, thereby mediating cardiopulmonary dysfunction. Existing studies have separately illustrated the roles of lactylation in isolated pulmonary and cardiac disorders. Nevertheless, most investigations are confined to a single-organ perspective, lacking systematic summaries of common mechanisms for cardiopulmonary crosstalk and comorbidities. The present review summarized research advances of lactylation in various cardiopulmonary diseases, generalized its potential comorbid mechanisms, identified existing research gaps and translational obstacles for targeted therapy and collected lactylation-targeted intervention compounds with potential therapeutic effects reported in basic studies. The present review further outlined prospective research directions focused on spatiotemporal regulation of lactylation, metabolic-immune-epigenetic crosstalk that shapes disease progression, and the identification of specific targets in cardiopulmonary comorbidities, with the aim of providing a theoretical foundation for developing precise, broad-spectrum, co-targeted therapeutic strategies for cardiopulmonary diseases.

title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
authors: Deshmukh K, Pandey M, Moulahoum H, Ghorbanizamani F, Kovářík T, Przekora-Kuśmierz A, Jena H, Vora M
abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

title: From biomarkers to therapeutic targets: Biomaterial-mediated cfDNA scavenging in inflammation.
authors: Liu S, Cheng X, Liu L, Luo E, Shao D, Huang H, Liu H
abstract: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) displays disease-dependent changes in abundance, fragmentation, composition, and tissue origin. Beyond serving as a noninvasive biomarker, persistent cfDNA can act as a damage-associated molecular pattern, activating TLR9, cGAS-STING, inflammasome signaling, and thromboinflammation. This review synthesizes advances in cfDNA biology, clinical applications, and therapeutic scavenging across inflammatory diseases. We critically evaluate the extent to which current clinical studies support diagnostic, prognostic, and causal conclusions while considering methodological heterogeneity. Particular emphasis is placed on how biomaterials transform cfDNA recognition into treatment. We trace the evolution from free nucleases and soluble cationic agents to nanostructured platforms that integrate DNA sequestration with retention, degradation, lesion targeting, or immunomodulation. Comparison of cationic polymers, dendrimers, core-shell nanoparticles, hydrogels, microneedles, nanosheets, and nuclease-enabled systems reveals how material architecture governs cfDNA accessibility, stability in biofluids, tissue distribution, and therapeutic efficacy. Localized and stimuli-responsive designs may improve selectivity and reduce systemic toxicity, but most efficacy evidence remains preclinical. Clinical translation therefore requires standardized cfDNA measurement, realistic biofluid testing, rigorous pharmacology, scalable manufacturing, and prospective demonstration that selective cfDNA removal improves outcomes without compromising host defense.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit for highly sensitive detection of aflatoxin B1.
authors: Wu Z, Ma Y, Li X, Yan Z, Huang Y, Wang K, Quan W, Mo L
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic mycotoxin and strongly carcinogenic and teratogenic to humans. Achieving CRISPR-based sensing system for highly sensitive detection of AFB1 remains a significant challenge. A CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit (CPSCN) is proposed for the sensitive and accurate detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). In the CPSCN sensing system, CRISPR/Cas12a/gRNA1 indirectly recognizes AFB1 by aptamer and effectively triggers trans-cleavage of a pair of self-reporting single-stranded DNA-locked RNA2 fluorescence probes (named as dual-winged fluorescence probe). The released RNA2 then initiates an autocatalytic positive feedback loop, resulting in continuous probe cleavage. The CPSCN system achieves highly sensitive detection in a single-enzyme one-step process. The method exhibits excellent quantitative capability for AFB1 detection with a detection limit of 7.5 pg/mL. In real samples, the detection results of the proposed biosensor show high consistency with those obtained by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). This work not only provides a novel strategy for AFB1 detection with high sensitivity, robustness, and operational simplicity, but also offers a new insight for designing signal amplification strategies of CRISPR-based biosensors.

title: Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis.
authors: Ai Y, Zhang Q, Chen T, Lin L, Chen Z, Liu G, Liu J, Dong Z
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. OBJECTIVE: To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. METHODS: SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. RESULTS: SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo, 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. CONCLUSION: The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

title: Machine learning models to predict pathological complete response after chemoradiotherapy in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: toward optimized indications for bladder preservation.
authors: Fujiwara M, Tanaka H, Hirahara D, Saho T, Takaya E, Matsumoto S, Yoshitomi K, Kobayashi M
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: After bladder-sparing chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC), residual microscopic disease may cause intravesical recurrence. This study aimed to develop machine learning models to predict pathological complete response (pCR) after CRT. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 285 patients with cT2-4N0M0 MIBC who underwent CRT followed by partial or radical cystectomy. CRT response was determined from cystectomy specimens. Patients were randomly assigned to a training cohort (n = 228) and a test cohort (n = 57) using a fixed random seed. A total of 102 machine learning models were evaluated in the training cohort. The model with the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) in the training-cohort was selected and then evaluated in the test cohort. The model incorporated clinical T stage, tumor size, multiplicity, hydronephrosis, bladder neck involvement (BNI), concomitant carcinoma in situ (CIS), variant histology, grade, and progression. RESULTS: Clinical T stages were T2/3/4 in 169/105/11 patients, respectively. Hydronephrosis was observed in 69 patients. Transurethral resection before CRT revealed multiplicity, BNI, and concomitant CIS in 108, 54, and 34 patients, respectively. Overall, 178/285 patients (62%) achieved pCR. WeightedEnsemble_L4 was selected as the final model and had a test-cohort AUC of 0.829 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.706-0.932). The calibration slope was 0.856 (95% CI, 0.469-1.639), and the wide CI indicated uncertainty in calibration. CONCLUSION: Machine learning based on clinicopathologic variables estimated pCR after CRT. This may support decision-making regarding bladder preservation in patients with MIBC.

title: Cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot enabling ultrasensitive one-pot detection of dual miRNAs in triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Yu L, Li X, Huang L
abstract: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are critical biomarkers for the early diagnosis of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but sensitive simultaneous detection of multiple miRNAs remains a clinical challenge. Herein, we report an innovative biosensing method based on a cascade DNA walker-driven photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot for one-pot, rapid, and ultrasensitive dual miRNA detection. Target miRNAs trigger the cascade DNA walker, which integrates catalytic hairpin assembly and enzyme-mediated strand displacement, to generate abundant single-stranded DNA (ssDNA). These ssDNA then activate the photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12a nanorobot under light illumination, enabling amplified fluorescence signaling for dual-target quantification. The assay exhibits a linear range of 100 aM to 1 pM with a limit of detection of 48.7 aM. Serum recovery experiments and cell line tests confirm its reliability in complex matrices. Clinical validation using 30 plasma samples (15 TNBC patients, 15 healthy controls) demonstrates high diagnostic accuracy (area under the curve, AUC = 0.964). This method features simple operation and strong clinical translational potential, offering a reliable tool for the early diagnosis of TNBC.

title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
authors: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D, He K, Chen Y, Li Y, Dai S, He Y
abstract: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) is a major pathogen responsible for adverse perinatal outcomes; rapid and accurate detection is crucial for preventing maternal-neonatal transmission and for guiding clinical interventions. Current GBS detection methods are limited by long assay times, insufficient sensitivity, and high equipment and operational requirements, restricting their application in resource-limited settings and rapid detection scenarios. Targeting the cfb gene of GBS, this study developed ERA-CasMNPs by integrating enzymatic recombinase amplification (ERA), CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated specific recognition and trans-cleavage activity of ssDNA, and horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-modified magnetic nanoparticle complexes (MNPs)-based colorimetric signal output. The ERA-CasMNPs biosensor enables rapid and sensitive visual detection of GBS within 85 min, with an LOD95 of 23.3 copies/μL (95% confidence interval: 15.6-34.8 copies/μL). Moreover, evaluation using 135 cultured clinical bacterial isolates demonstrated that ERA-CasMNPs achieved a sensitivity of 97.33%, a specificity of 98.33%, and a detection accuracy of 97.78%, comparable to qPCR. These results indicate that the ERA-CasMNPs biosensor provides a sensitive and visual method for rapid detection of GBS and supports its potential for further evaluation in resource-limited and rapid-testing settings.

title: Identification of neoechinulin B metabolites in vivo by UPLC Q/TOF MS and exploration of its anti HCV mechanism based on network pharmacology and molecular docking.
authors: Ren X, Lu XH, Chen YF, Tu XP, Li BY, Tao X, Yang X, Zhang FX
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: Fungal secondary metabolites, owing to their structural diversity and broad spectrum of bioactivities, have become a vital source for the discovery of microbial drugs and antiviral lead compounds. Fungi of the genus Aspergillus, which are ubiquitous filamentous microorganisms, are capable of producing structurally novel and functionally diverse secondary metabolites, thus representing a rich reservoir for drug lead discovery. Neoechinulin B (NeoB), an isoprenyl indole diketopiperazine alkaloid isolated from Aspergillus strains, exhibits potent antiviral activity. However, its poor characterization in terms of in vivo metabolism has hindered further development. In this work, we systematically explored the metabolic profile of NeoB in Sprague-Dawley rats, and combined network pharmacology with molecular docking to generate hypotheses regarding its potential anti‑HCV mechanism. These computational results are predictive and require future experimental validation. Following oral administration of NeoB to rats at 20 mg/kg/day, a total of 18 compounds, including NeoB and its metabolites, were identified in plasma, urine, faeces, heart, and liver. The proposed major metabolic pathways involved demethylation, sulfation, and glucuronidation. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were then used to generate hypotheses regarding potential anti-HCV targets. These computational results are predictive and require future experimental validation. Network pharmacology suggested that NeoB and its representative metabolites may potentially modulate targets such as SRC and EGFR, and by interfering with signalling pathways including "Proteoglycans in cancer" and "Hepatitis C". Molecular docking results suggested a potential preference for SRC over EGFR based on docking scores. However, because redocking validation for EGFR and SRC did not meets the 2.0 Å threshold, theses docking scores are considered computational estimates only. They cannot be used to infer target selectivity or differences in binding affinity. The parent compound P0 showed lowest docking score with SRC (-10.5 kcal/mol)), but this value is a computational estimate and does not represent experimental binding affinity. Overall, the docking outcomes were consistent with the network pharmacology predictions. This study qualitatively characterizes the in vivo metabolic profile of NeoB and provides computational hypotheses for future research. Any therapeutic implications remain speculative.

title: Spatial organization of magnetic nanoparticles in chitosan-gelatin hydrogels enables enhanced magnetic actuation and cell response under dynamic stimulation.
authors: Viteri A, Ginebra MP, García-Torres J
abstract: Magnetically responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for remotely modulating HFF-1 fibroblasts behavior through dynamic mechanical stimulation; however, the influence of magnetic nanoparticle spatial organization on magnetic actuation and cell response remains unexplored. Herein, we report the development of chitosan-gelatin magnetic hydrogels with controlled Fe3O4 nanoparticle distribution including homogeneously dispersed, and spatially patterned configurations, as a strategy to engineer localized mechanotransduction and magnetic actuation. The role of nanoparticle organization on the physicochemical, magnetic, and biological properties of the hydrogels has been analyzed. Structural characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of Fe3O4 nanoparticles while preserving their crystalline inverse spinel structure. Morphological and topographical analyses revealed that patterned hydrogels exhibit well-defined nanoparticle-rich and nanoparticle-free regions, generating pronounced microscale heterogeneity throughout the material. The incorporation and spatial confinement of Fe3O4 nanoparticles significantly influenced the hydrogel properties, increasing stiffness, reducing swelling capacity, and enhancing magnetic responsiveness. Notably, patterned hydrogels displayed higher saturation magnetization and magnetic susceptibility than homogeneously dispersed systems, indicating that nanoparticle confinement promotes cooperative magnetic interactions and more efficient magnetic actuation. Biological studies demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility for all hydrogel formulations. While static magnetic stimulation slightly reduced fibroblast proliferation, dynamic magnetic stimulation significantly enhanced cell proliferation, spreading, and cytoskeletal organization, particularly in patterned hydrogels. These effects are attributed to cyclic mechanical cues generated by amplified magnetic-to-mechanical transduction within the patterned magnetic domains. Overall, this study demonstrates that nanoparticle spatial organization is a key design parameter for engineering magnetically responsive hydrogels with tunable magnetic actuation and controllable cellular responses for tissue engineering applications.

title: Echo-DM: Ultrasound marker removal via conditional latent diffusion and region-aware fusion.
authors: Wang Z, Huang T, Jiang W, Li M, Liu J, Chen J, Zou J, Luo Y
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Clinical ultrasound images often contain artificial markers, such as measurement calipers and text, to assist diagnostic interpretation and comparison. However, these markers can introduce shortcut bias in downstream automated analysis, encouraging deep learning models to rely on marker-related cues rather than clinically meaningful anatomy. Existing marker removal methods are either mask-dependent and vulnerable to error propagation, or mask-free deterministic restorers that may over-smooth ultrasound texture and perturb unaffected background regions. To address these challenges, we present Echo-DM, a framework for ultrasound marker removal via conditional latent diffusion and region-aware fusion. Echo-DM follows a generate-select-refine formulation: a DiT-based Conditional Latent Diffusion Network (CLDN) generates an intermediate restoration, and a Region-Aware Fusion (RAF) module internally predicts a soft map to selectively fuse the restoration with intact input content before residual refinement in image space under end-to-end mask-free inference. The image-space RAF is latent-module-agnostic and is shared by Echo-DM-V and Echo-DM-R, which use VAE-based and RAE-based latent modules, respectively. Extensive experiments on Echo-PAIR, a large-scale paired clinical ultrasound dataset, demonstrate superior marker removal and strong anatomical fidelity compared with representative two-stage baselines, while providing favorable quality-efficiency trade-offs across deployment settings. Code and models will be released at Echo-DM.

title: Neurosurgical scalp incisions should preserve at least one vascular axis: Two case reports.
authors: Lupon E, Hertzog B, Njessi P, Camuzard O
abstract: BACKGROUND: Scalp necrosis after neurosurgery is usually attributed to repeated surgery. We report two cases in which necrosis was precipitated by a single reoperation incision that disregarded scalp arterial anatomy and the previous scars, and describe how this dictated the reconstruction. CASES: Case 1: a 56-year-old woman underwent emergency decompressive hemicraniectomy two days after meningioma resection, through a circumferential incision along the bone-flap margin that islanded the cutaneous flap from every axial pedicle; the whole hemiscalp necrosed with brain exposure. Case 2: a 15-year-old boy, operated on repeatedly for subdural empyema, underwent cranioplasty through an incision that transected the superficial temporal pedicle, the last axis supplying a scalp segment already isolated by previous incisions. In both cases the extent of necrosis and the absence of any remaining axial pedicle precluded local, regional or expanded flaps; a free latissimus dorsi muscle flap anastomosed to the superficial temporal vessels was the only option. Hair restoration in Case 2 was completed by follicular unit extraction onto the flap. CONCLUSIONS: A scalp flap survives only if at least one axial pedicle enters its base. Neurosurgical incisions, particularly at reoperation, should be drawn on the arterial map and previous scars; plastic and neurosurgical teams should share this rule.

title: Three-dimensional and dynamic assessment of digital lymphatic vessels using photoacoustic imaging.
authors: Suzuki Y, Uno T, Kajita H, Kato T, Takatsume Y, Imanishi N, Kishi K
abstract: Digital lymphatic anatomy has been defined largely by cadaveric studies. We evaluated whether photoacoustic lymphangiography (PAL) could depict three-dimensional anatomy and motion-related deformation in vivo. Two healthy volunteers and one patient with secondary upper-extremity lymphedema underwent fingertip indocyanine green injection, near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and static and dynamic PAL. In healthy fingers, lymphatic vessels coursed mainly along the lateral aspects toward the dorsal hand and lay between superficial veins and digital arteries. Flexion produced spiral-like deformation or abrupt angulation, whereas vessels were relatively straight during extension; segmental lymphatic signals moved proximally during motion. In the patient, PAL visualized vessels beneath dermal backflow that appeared more irregular and showed frequent short-segment tortuosity, and guided lymphaticovenular anastomosis. These findings support the feasibility of finger-specific, in vivo three-dimensional and motion-resolved assessment of digital lymphatic morphology using PAL.

title: Effects of sitagliptin combined with GTS-21 on improving glycemic control and diabetic nephropathy by anti-apoptosis in Leprdb/db mice.
authors: Tian W, Wang W, Tang S, Su L, Cooney R, Tian X, Meng Q
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Activation of α7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (α7nAChR) by GTS-21 engages the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway (CAP). This study investigated adding GTS-21 to sitagliptin, a DPP-4 inhibitor used to increase endogenous GLP-1, confers additional benefit over sitagliptin monotherapy on glycemic control and diabetic nephropathy (DN) in Leprdb/db mice, focusing on anti-apoptotic mechanisms. METHODS: Leptin receptor-deficient (Leprdb/db, 8-week-old) mice were randomized into control (saline), sitagliptin (20 mg/kg), or combination (sitagliptin 20 mg/kg + GTS-21 4 mg/kg) groups for 4 weeks. Oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT), serum creatinine (Scr), blood urea nitrogen (BUN), and IL-6 were measured. Renal histology was evaluated by H&E staining. Apoptosis was assessed by TUNEL staining and cleaved caspase-3 expression. In vitro, HK-2 cells exposed to high glucose (30 mM) were treated with liraglutide (100 nM) and/or GTS-21 (20 nM) to examine apoptosis. RESULTS: Combination therapy significantly improved glucose tolerance at weeks 1 and 4 (AUC reduction, P = 0.0366 and P = 0.0435 vs control), whereas sitagliptin alone showed no effect. Both treatments reduced Scr (P = 0.0002 for combination; P = 0.0101 for monotherapy), but only combination therapy attenuated renal histological injury (P = 0.002) and decreased IL-6 in serum and kidney (P = 0.0433 and P = 0.0041). Renal apoptosis was also suppressed, with reduced TUNEL-positive cells (P = 0.0043) and cleaved caspase-3 (P = 0.0122). In HK-2 cells, high glucose increased cleaved caspase-3 (P = 0.0324), which was attenuated by liraglutide plus GTS-21 (P = 0.0320). CONCLUSIONS: Add-on GTS-21 to sitagliptin improved glycemic control and attenuated diabetic nephropathy beyond sitagliptin monotherapy in Leprdb/db mice, with reduced renal inflammation and suppressed apoptosis. These findings suggest that combined activation of GLP-1 receptor and α7nAChR signaling warrants further investigation as a renoprotective strategy in diabetic nephropathy.

title: Interstitial Molar Ectopic Pregnancy Despite Euploid Embryo Transfer: A Case Report.
authors: Patel K, Sakkas D, Groszmann Y, Murphy L, Penzias A, Dottino J
abstract: BACKGROUND: Even with modern in vitro fertilization (IVF) techniques, unexpected pregnancy outcomes can occur. Molar pregnancy after IVF and embryo transfer can be the result of true abnormal fertilization in the embryology lab. Preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies (PGT-A) has advanced and is widely used, but unless additional testing of single-nucleotide polymorphisms is performed, the rare case of partial molar pregnancy (defined as triploidy of paternal origin) after IVF may be missed. Unexpected pregnancy outcomes may also be a result of spontaneous fertilization during assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment. CASE: The patient is a 36-year-old G1P100 who initially underwent IVF and intracytoplasmic sperm injection with PGT-A and preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic disorders for galactosemia carrier status in both partners. After obtaining euploid and galactosemia unaffected embryos, she underwent a frozen embryo transfer of a female, euploid embryo. The result was a right interstitial molar ectopic pregnancy that was managed with laparoscopic right cornual resection. CONCLUSION: Assisted reproductive technology with PGT-A attempts to eliminate the risk of abnormal embryo transfer. Technical factors, such as variations in testing processes among PGT-A laboratories, and human factors, such as unprotected intercourse during ART, contribute to unexpected pregnancy outcomes.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism.
authors: Ahamba IS, Song G, Kinkpe L, Duan Q, Goswami N, Jin Z, Wu J, Dong X
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) significantly influences meat quality, affecting flavor, tenderness, and juiciness. Despite extensive research on livestock such as cattle and pigs, the regulation of IMF in rabbits remains poorly understood. This study establishes a standardized in vitro method for isolating and characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes from the longissimus dorsi muscle of 3-day-old Hycole rabbits using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation. Three-day-old neonates were selected for initial protocol development due to their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields. Isolated cells displayed typical preadipocyte morphology and expressed key markers, including PREF-1, PPARγ, and Leptin, confirmed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. Upon adipogenic induction, cells exhibited progressive lipid accumulation, as indicated by Oil Red O staining, and showed upregulated expression of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, confirming their differentiation potential. This study establishes a comprehensive protocol for isolating rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes, providing a foundational tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms of adipogenesis in lagomorphs. The model supports future studies on genetic and nutritional strategies to enhance rabbit meat quality while preserving its lean characteristics.

title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Zhu J, Zhong Y, Yan S, Zeng X
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo, FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

title: Coacervate protocells-mediated mitochondrial transplantation restores gut epithelial energetic homeostasis in ulcerative colitis.
authors: Ding B, Chen Y, Jia Y, Li J, Tan Z, Wu W, Ouyang S, Tong B
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction in intestinal epithelial cells, yet current therapies fail to correct underlying energy metabolism defects. While exogenous mitochondrial transplantation offers a promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by rapid loss of mitochondrial bioactivity ex vivo, poor delivery efficiency, and lysosomal degradation following cellular uptake. Here, we developed a biomimetic coacervate-based protocell system (HTP) via liquid-liquid phase separation of polyethylene glycol, tannic acid, and sodium hyaluronate for efficient encapsulation and delivery of functional mitochondria (HTP@Mito). HTP protocells preserved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis capacity for up to 72 h in HBSS buffer at 37°C, far exceeding the viability of free mitochondria. Notably, HTP markedly enhanced intracellular delivery of isolated mitochondria via lipid-raft-mediated endocytosis. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine UC model, rectally administrating HTP@Mito achieved superior therapeutic efficacy via restoring ATP levels and mitochondrial membrane potential, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, by reducing oxidative stress, HTP@Mito rescued lysosomal function and restored impaired autophagic flux, thereby promoting mitophagy to clear damaged mitochondria. HTP@Mito treatment also repaired intestinal epithelial tight junctions, restored goblet cell-derived mucus secretion, and rebalanced gut microbiota by increasing beneficial Lachnospiraceae while reducing pathogenic Escherichia-Shigella. Collectively, this work established a versatile, biomimetic organelle delivery platform that could correct mitochondrial energy deficiency in the intestinal epithelium, providing a framework for mitochondrial transplantation in ulcerative colitis.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: Oxygen-vacancy-rich LDH sonosensitizers potentiate narrow-spectrum antibiotics via membrane-disruption strategy for mixed bacterial wound infections.
authors: Xi L, Liu X, Yu C, Wang T, Liao J, Lv Y, Zhang M, Zhang Y
abstract: Mixed bacterial infections, including Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens, remain a major global health concern. Achieving efficient treatment of synergistic polymicrobial infections stills a tremendous clinical challenge due to antibiotic permeability barriers and resistance. Here, we construct a defect-engineered layered double hydroxide (LDH)-based sonosensitizer platform loaded with clindamycin (a-CoW/CLD) for mixed bacterial infection therapy, which not only demonstrates high efficacy against Gram-positive bacteria, but also exploits reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated membrane disruption of Gram-negative bacteria to facilitate CLD penetration, thereby achieving broad-spectrum and highly efficient killing of mixed bacteria. The amorphous a-CoW nanosheets, enriched with oxygen vacancies via acid etching, exhibit a substantially narrowed bandgap (1.22 eV) and markedly enhanced charge separation, producing 22.1-fold higher singlet oxygen under ultrasound (US) irradiation compared with pristine CoW. This ROS burst synergized with CLD achieves potent killing of Staphylococcus aureus (>99.9% at 20 μg mL-1). More critically, ROS disrupt the outer membrane of Gram-negative Escherichia coli, promoting CLD internalization and consequently boosting its lethality by 18.4-fold (from ∼5% to >92.1%). Mechanistic transcriptomics reveals ROS and CLD synergy: ROS disrupt the bacterial membrane via lipid peroxidation, enabling CLD penetration to block protein synthesis and metabolism, while ROS also induce oxidative stress, collectively leading to bacterial death. In a murine wound model co-infected with both pathogens, a-CoW/CLD plus US eradicates >99.9% of mixed bacteria, suppresses systemic inflammation, and significantly accelerates angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. This paradigm establishes a low-dose, broad-spectrum sonodynamic-antibiotic strategy that overcomes antibiotic permeability bottleneck, offering a promising therapeutic avenue against mixed bacterial infections.

A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
authors: Su W, Zhang X, Li R, Li K, Guo X, Liu X, Wang Z, Wang H
abstract: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Systems pharmacology reveals the molecular mechanisms of nerolidol against polycystic ovary syndrome through integrated transcriptomic, network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Kumar GS, Soni A, Pattanayak N, Morie F, Baldaniya LH
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is a heterogeneous endocrine and metabolic disorder marked by hyperandrogenism, ovulatory dysfunction, insulin resistance, chronic inflammation and oxidative stress, arising from dysregulation across several interconnected molecular pathways. Because its pathogenesis is multifactorial, therapies targeting diverse biological processes at once remain scarce. Nerolidol, a naturally occurring sesquiterpene alcohol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and cytoprotective properties, has an action against PCOS whose molecular basis remains unresolved. Transcriptomic differences associated with PCOS were examined using the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) dataset GSE34526. Exploratory differential-expression screening identified nominally altered probes using an unadjusted P < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1; however, no individual probe remained significant after Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR < 0.05. Functional enrichment analysis was subsequently used to investigate biological processes and pathways represented by these exploratory transcriptional signals. Gene Ontology (GO) and KEGG enrichment were applied to pinpoint dysregulated biological processes and signalling pathways. Computational findings were tested in a letrozole-induced PCOS rat model treated with nerolidol, with efficacy judged from oestrous cyclicity, ovarian histopathology, reproductive hormone profiles, oxidative stress biomarkers, inflammatory mediators and metabolic parameters. Transcriptomic analysis showed marked enrichment of processes related to kinase regulation, insulin secretion, intrinsic apoptotic signalling, receptor-mediated signalling and the DNA damage response, while KEGG analysis pointed to pathways governing endocrine regulation, cell signalling and metabolic homeostasis. In animal experiments, nerolidol restored oestrous cyclicity, improved ovarian morphology, corrected endocrine disturbances, and reduced oxidative stress and PCOS-related pathology. These phenotypic effects were functionally concordant with several biological processes highlighted by the computational analyses. However, because the predicted signalling molecules and pathways were not directly measured in ovarian tissue following nerolidol treatment, the proposed molecular mechanisms remain hypotheses requiring targeted experimental validation.
